requirements.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b
requirements.summary: node1's opt1 (vtnet1, 10.60.1.1/24) and opt2 (vtnet2, 10.60.2.1/24) interfaces were configured and confirmed up; node2 (10.60.1.2) and node3 (10.60.2.2) were placed on the respective subnets with static routes via node1, ARP table confirmed both peers reachable on the correct interfaces, and cross-LAN ICMP ping between node2 and node3 succeeded through node1 both before and after all three nodes were restarted.

requirements.requirement: Refuse TCP port 23 between the two networks
requirements.summary: pf block rules for tcp/23 were added on both opt1 (vtnet1) and opt2 (vtnet2) and verified present in the active ruleset; live connection attempts on port 23 from node2->node3 and node3->node2 both timed out (blocked), confirmed again after restarts of all nodes.

requirements.requirement: Record every refused attempt in a log on node1
requirements.summary: filterlog entries in /var/log/filter/filter_20260905.log show 'block' action with the telnet-rule label for blocked port-23 SYNs in both directions (10.60.1.2->10.60.2.2 and 10.60.2.2->10.60.1.2), including fresh entries captured after node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Show a log entry produced by an attempt made from node2
requirements.summary: A specific filterlog line (sequenceId 38/39) shows src 10.60.1.2 (node2) -> dst 10.60.2.2 (node3), port 23, action=block, matching the telnet block rule label on vtnet1, directly correlated with the telnet attempt executed from node2 in cmd-e33fdf392ecc436d.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on every managed node
requirements.summary: For all three nodes, pre-restart boot identity and healthy state were captured, a restart was explicitly acknowledged, a differing post-restart boot identity was observed (node1 kern.boottime 1788629261->1788629665; node2 boot_id 377b5195...->a2597d9a...; node3 boot_id 583ddd53...->c043a424...), and recovered service/data/cluster state (interfaces, pf rules, routes, cross-LAN ping, and telnet block+log behavior) was re-verified after each restart. The fixed lifecycle after_executor snapshot independently corroborates the same boot-identity transitions for all three nodes.

overall_summary: All four material task outcomes are directly satisfied: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b, TCP/23 is blocked and logged on node1 in both directions, and a specific filterlog entry produced by a node2-originated telnet attempt is shown. The executor additionally ran and documented a complete provider-wide restart-evidence protocol on all three nodes, with pre/post boot-identity, acknowledgement, and recovered-state evidence for each, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is good: the few failed or exploratory commands (an unsupported configctl call, invalid-gateway route attempts, a missing-binary nc attempt, a timed-out background tcpdump) caused no persisted state and were either inherently inert or explicitly cleaned up.
limitations: The pf rule set uses one shared block rule per interface (opt1/opt2) rather than one keyed strictly to lan-a<->lan-b direction pairs; since only node2 (lan-a) and node3 (lan-b) are attached to these interfaces, this is functionally equivalent for this topology but wasn't independently tested against a third host on the same segment.
Boot-identity and recovery evidence for restarts relies on SSH/command reachability polling rather than an independent out-of-band health check, though this is consistent with the available toolset.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor mutations were overwhelmingly tied to satisfying the task or the restart protocol: config.xml interface/pf rule edits (backed up first via config.xml.bak.pretask), configctl reconfigure/reload calls, node2/node3 IP assignment (first via transient 'ip addr add', later superseded by persistent nmcli lan-a/lan-b profiles needed to survive reboot), and the three controlled reboots. Several commands failed without mutating state and left no residue: configctl interface reload (cmd-282430801b0e4fb9, unsupported action), ip route add attempts with invalid-gateway errors (cmd-4904e0147eda4b52, cmd-0544bad9e1824885), and an nc listener attempt on node3 that failed because nc was not installed (cmd-aa7cf22692314e50). A backgrounded tcpdump diagnostic on node1 (cmd-44f8a9ec24bb48e9) caused a 120s proxy timeout but was a bounded, read-only capture that was cleanly killed with pkill (cmd-4e4327a624df42f2), leaving no persistent state. Lifecycle temp-file diffs on all nodes show only expected reboot-churn (systemd-private dirs keyed to the new boot id, /tmp/reboot.log) and OPNsense's own transient tmpcfd_*/tmpHOSTS files from configctl activity, not executor-created residue.
